claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the distinguished-point Teske 16-adding walk in proof.md (full subgroup, no negation quotient and no GLV endomorphism, 4096 parallel walks, Montgomery batch of width 4096, distinguished modulus 2^16, open-addressed table of 2^116 slots with probe cap 80) recovers x with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^128.931657 total target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 with C=1000, including preprocessing, the incomplete-addition reserve, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^123.584963 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^111.034216 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Heuristics and their slack are those listed in claim.json. This is a classical cold attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustive recovery on Z/n under the same 16 branch multipliers, the same 64-bit mix and the same 3/2 birthday budget as proof.md. Distinguished-point filtering is off below modulus 2^16 so the relation is checked on every iterate. Does not establish production instruction costs, probe-chain lengths or secp256k1 field arithmetic.
